# B2 Reference Architectures for Image Generation: full text

> Generated by tools/generate_catalog.py from the pages listed below; links are relative to the repository root. Product behavior is authoritative at https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning.

<!-- source: docs/image-generation.md -->

# Image generation on Backblaze B2 (agent-readable)

Catalog updated: 2026-11-16. Current product behavior is authoritative in the [Backblaze B2 documentation](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage).

## Workload
Image generation teams curate image-text corpora, fine-tune diffusion models (LoRA, DreamBooth, full fine-tunes), distribute base checkpoints and LoRAs to GPU inference fleets, generate images through self-hosted pipelines or hosted APIs, accept user-uploaded reference images, and serve galleries. Object storage holds training shards, embeddings, checkpoints, released weights, generated outputs with provenance manifests, moderated uploads and gallery originals.

## Where does B2 fit?
B2 is the durable system of record for training data, model weights and generated outputs, reached through the S3-compatible endpoint `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` (derive the region from the bucket; never hardcode it). Two category facts favor it: hosted output URLs are ephemeral (Replicate deletes API output files after one hour), so outputs need a durable store; and galleries are read-heavy, so a private B2 origin behind a CDN partner with free egress keeps delivery costs predictable.

## Which tools connect, and how?

Configure each integration with the B2 regional endpoint, bucket region, addressing style, and scoped credentials specified in its setup guide.

- **Built-in Backblaze B2 option:** MLflow (`b2://` artifact URI), rclone, ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes, hf-cache-sync, Pixeltable.
- **S3 custom endpoint:** Ray Train (`endpoint_override`), DVC, LanceDB, Modal `CloudBucketMount`, WebDataset (S3 client behind gopen), Uppy Companion, imgproxy, Cloudflare Workers.
- **CDN origin:** bunny.net uses S3 Authentication for the private B2 origin.
- **fsspec / s3fs:** img2dataset, s3fs.
- **Presigned URLs:** fal.ai and Replicate take inputs by URL; pass short-expiry presigned B2 GET URLs and copy outputs back to B2.

## B2 capabilities that apply
S3-compatible API; prefix-scoped application keys; multipart upload for shards and checkpoints; presigned URLs (provider handoff, browser uploads, private sharing) and CORS; Event Notifications (signed webhooks for moderation, indexing, CDN purge); versions and lifecycle rules (expire checkpoints, drafts, raw uploads by prefix); SSE-B2; Object Lock default retention on dedicated raw-corpus, released-weights and audit buckets, per-file retention on released weights in the models bucket; Cloud Replication for a second-region disaster-recovery copy; CDN partner delivery and included egress under the [current pricing terms](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing).

## Reference architectures

- [image-text-corpus-curation](architectures/image-text-corpus-curation/architecture.md): img2dataset writes WebDataset shards to a locked raw bucket; scoring writes stats, embeddings and parquet exclusion lists; filtered subsets are new shards with a manifest written last.
- [diffusion-finetune-checkpoints](architectures/diffusion-finetune-checkpoints/architecture.md): Ray Train or rclone-synced trainers write `checkpoints/<run_id>/` (lifecycle-expired) and `runs/<run_id>/final/`; MLflow and DVC track artifacts; released weights go to a locked bucket.
- [model-weight-distribution](architectures/model-weight-distribution/architecture.md): CI publishes immutable versioned weights with a `latest.json` pointer; ComfyUI nodes, hf-cache-sync, Modal mounts and rclone pull into node-local caches with read-only keys.
- [generation-output-provenance](architectures/generation-output-provenance/architecture.md): every output and its SHA-256 manifest (provider, model, prompt, params, seed, parent) is written to B2 at once; hosted APIs get presigned inputs.
- [user-upload-moderation-personalization](architectures/user-upload-moderation-personalization/architecture.md): presigned browser uploads, event-driven moderation and EXIF stripping, presigned handoff to edit and LoRA-training APIs, subject deletion across all B2 versions (including quarantine), in-flight jobs, and provider copies; no Object Lock.
- [gallery-cdn-delivery](architectures/gallery-cdn-delivery/architecture.md): private bucket behind a Cloudflare Worker or bunny.net S3-authenticated pull zone; imgproxy renders variants that the CDN caches.

## When Overdrive may apply
Sustained multi-node shard reads during training, or fleet-wide cold starts pulling the same multi-GB weights at once, where measured object throughput (not GPU or network) is the bottleneck. Node-local caches come first. Confirm with [B2 Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive). Not relevant to per-image generation or gallery requests.

## Where B2 does not fit
GPU memory and node-local model directories the runtime loads from; active training scratch and in-progress checkpoint writes; live vector indexes that serve queries; app, user, billing, moderation, registry and MLflow backend databases; queues and caches; CDN edge caches; C2PA signing keys. Trainers that write only to local disk (diffusers example scripts, kohya sd-scripts) need an rclone sync step. Cloud Replication is bucket-to-bucket, not delivery.

## Links
[README](README.md) - [Architecture index](docs/architecture-index.md) - [Related B2 samples](docs/related-b2-samples.md) - [B2 configuration examples](examples/README.md) - [B2 docs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage) - [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) - [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api) - [Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide) - [Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock) - [Awesome Image Generation](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/awesome-image-generation)

<!-- source: architectures/image-text-corpus-curation/architecture.md -->

# Collect and curate image-text corpora into streamable training shards

## Workload

Text-to-image models train on image-text pairs: crawled URL and caption lists, licensed collections, or both. A curation team downloads them into tar shards, scores every pair (CLIP similarity, aesthetic or quality score, NSFW probability, near-duplicate clusters) and produces filtered subsets defined by a recipe. Several recipes are compared, so the raw pool must stay fixed and every subset must be reproducible.

B2 holds the raw shards, per-sample scores, embeddings, exclusion lists and filtered subsets. Queues, catalogs, live vector serving and GPU-local caches stay elsewhere.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  URLS[URL + caption lists] -->|S3 API| RAWU[(corpus-raw<br/>raw/corpus/urls/)]
  RAWU --> DL[img2dataset<br/>fsspec s3 endpoint = B2]
  DL -->|multipart PUT| RAWS[(corpus-raw<br/>raw/corpus/shards/*.tar<br/>Object Lock)]
  RAWS -->|stream shards| SCORE[Scoring workers<br/>CLIP / Data-Juicer / NSFW / fastdup]
  SCORE --> STATS[(corpus-work<br/>stats/run/)]
  SCORE --> EMB[(corpus-work<br/>embeddings/job/)]
  SCORE --> EXCL[(corpus-work<br/>quarantine/run/*.parquet)]
  RAWS -->|stream + exclusion list| PACK[Re-pack kept samples]
  EXCL --> PACK
  PACK -->|shards, then manifest last| FILT[(corpus-work<br/>filtered/recipe-version/)]
  FILT -->|WebDataset s3:// opener| TRAIN[Diffusion training]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Re-pack job
  participant B as B2 corpus-work
  participant T as Trainer
  P->>B: PUT filtered/<recipe-version>/00000.tar ... N.tar
  P->>B: PUT filtered/<recipe-version>/subset-manifest.json (last)
  T->>B: GET subset-manifest.json
  alt manifest present
    T->>B: GET shards listed in manifest (per-worker, per-node split)
  else manifest missing
    T-->>T: subset incomplete; do not train
  end
```

Samples inside a tar shard cannot be server-side copied one by one, so curation never edits raw shards. Excluded sample keys go to parquet exclusion lists; filtered subsets are new shards. Server-side-copy quarantine applies only to loose files (see the fastdup and CLIP moderation samples).

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-imggen-corpus-raw` | `raw/<corpus>/urls/`, `raw/<corpus>/shards/` | Keep all versions; no expiry | Governance default retention (bucket-level) | Immutable raw pool and download stats |
| `<org>-imggen-corpus-work` | `stats/<run>/` | Hide after N days, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-corpus-work.json)) | No | Per-sample scores, re-computable |
| `<org>-imggen-corpus-work` | `embeddings/<job>/` | Keep while a subset depends on it | No | `.npy` shards or a LanceDB table |
| `<org>-imggen-corpus-work` | `quarantine/<run>/` | Keep | No | Parquet exclusion lists (sample keys + reason) |
| `<org>-imggen-corpus-work` | `filtered/<recipe-version>/` | Never overwrite; new recipe = new prefix | Optional: move released subsets to a locked bucket | Training subsets + `subset-manifest.json` |

Object Lock and default retention are bucket-level settings, which is why the raw pool gets its own bucket. Lifecycle rules match by file-name prefix, so data that expires sits under its own top-level prefix and nothing that must be kept shares it.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Job and shard queue | Ray or Redis | Needs atomic claims and low latency |
| Crawl dedup and robots cache | Key-value store | Per-request lookups |
| Dataset catalog (corpus records, licenses, recipe-to-subset mapping) | Postgres or similar | Relational queries and edits |
| Live vector index serving similarity queries | In-memory FAISS or a vector DB service | Query latency; B2 keeps the durable embedding files |
| Read-ahead cache for active shards | GPU-node NVMe | Repeated epochs over the same subset |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Status | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Used | All tools reach B2 through `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | Used (alternative) | Presigned HTTPS shard URLs for jobs that cannot hold keys; no browser access, so no CORS |
| Multipart upload | Used | Shards of roughly 0.3-1 GB |
| Scoped application keys | Used | `ingest-writer`, `curation`, `training-reader` (below) |
| Event Notifications | Not used | Curation runs are batch-scheduled |
| Object versions | Used | Raw bucket keeps versions; filtered subsets are never overwritten |
| Lifecycle rules | Used | Expire `stats/` scores that can be recomputed |
| SSE-B2 | Optional | Enable when corpora include licensed or sensitive data ([example](examples/sse.json)) |
| Object Lock | Used | Raw-corpus bucket only ([example](examples/object-lock.json)) |
| Cloud Replication | Not used | Re-downloadable raw data rarely justifies a second copy; add for licensed collections |
| Egress / CDN / compute partners | Situational | Place scoring and training compute near the bucket region; see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for egress terms |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard default | Consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) only when measured multi-node shard reads are the training bottleneck; add NVMe read-ahead for repeated epochs |

## Integration configuration

All endpoints are derived from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Never copy a region from an example.

### img2dataset (fsspec)

The img2dataset README documents writing to S3-compatible stores through fsspec: set `output_folder` to `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>` and put the endpoint in `~/.config/fsspec/s3.json`:

```json
{"s3": {"client_kwargs": {"endpoint_url": "https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com"}}}
```

Credentials come from the standard AWS environment variables holding a B2 application key. Use `output_format` `webdataset` or `parquet`; the `tfrecord` writer does not go through fsspec.

### s3fs (fsspec)

`S3FileSystem(endpoint_url="https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com", key=..., secret=...)` is the shared layer for scoring and re-packing jobs. Give each job a B2 application key scoped to the prefixes it reads and writes.

### WebDataset

WebDataset opens shards through gopen (`pipe:` and HTTP URLs), so configure the B2 endpoint in the S3 client it calls. The [Backblaze streaming sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training) registers a custom `s3://` opener backed by a boto3 client at the B2 endpoint and splits shards per worker and per node. A `pipe:aws s3 cp --endpoint-url https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com s3://<bucket>/<shard>.tar -` URL or presigned HTTPS shard URLs work the same way.

### LanceDB

Use the [pinned LanceDB connection profile](examples/lancedb.md) for embedding tables in the corpus-work bucket. It specifies the B2 endpoint, region, credentials and a Lance version whose S3 commit handler requires one writer per table. Serialize ingest, index creation, compaction and other mutations through one writer service. Readers can run separately; serve live queries from a separate index if latency matters. Endpoint settings alone do not establish safe commit behavior across Lance versions.

### Scoped keys

| Role | Bucket | Prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ingest-writer` | corpus-raw | `raw/` | `listFiles,writeFiles` |
| `curation` | corpus-work | (bucket) | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| `curation-raw-reader` | corpus-raw | `raw/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| `training-reader` | corpus-work | `filtered/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| `takedown-admin` (provisioning only) | corpus-raw | `raw/` | `listFiles,readFiles,deleteFiles,bypassGovernance` |

This design restricts each standard application key to one bucket and one file-name prefix, so a job that reads raw and writes work holds two keys. (B2 also offers multi-bucket keys; least privilege here relies on prefixes.) See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md) for the commands.

## Security

- No runtime key can delete raw shards; Object Lock enforces it even if a key leaks.
- Takedowns are honoured through exclusion lists and new subsets. When a legal takedown requires deleting a raw object, the separately held `takedown-admin` key uses `bypassGovernance`; runtime keys never hold that capability.
- Training jobs hold read-only keys for `filtered/` only.
- Presigned shard URLs are bearer credentials; keep TTLs to the job duration and never log them.
- Keep keys in a gitignored `0600` `.env` or a secret store.

## References

- [img2dataset](https://github.com/rom1504/img2dataset)
- [s3fs documentation](https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)
- [WebDataset](https://github.com/webdataset/webdataset)
- [Lance S3 commit-handler implementation for the pinned profile](https://github.com/lance-format/lance/blob/v0.23.2/rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)

<!-- source: architectures/diffusion-finetune-checkpoints/architecture.md -->

# Fine-tune LoRA and diffusion models with versioned checkpoints

## Workload

Teams fine-tune diffusion models (LoRA, DreamBooth or full fine-tunes of SD-family or FLUX-family models) on curated subsets. A run produces a dataset snapshot and captions, periodic checkpoints (MB-scale for LoRA adapters, tens of GB with full weights and optimizer state), sample grids for visual review, and final `.safetensors` weights. Runs often use spot or preemptible GPUs, so they must resume from the latest checkpoint, and released weights must trace back to the data that produced them.

B2 holds snapshots, checkpoints, samples, final weights and MLflow artifacts. Active training scratch, the MLflow backend database and the scheduler stay elsewhere.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SUB[(corpus-work<br/>filtered/recipe-version/)] -->|snapshot ref + captions| SNAP[(training<br/>runs/run_id/dataset/)]
  SNAP --> TRAIN[Trainer<br/>Ray Train or diffusers / kohya]
  TRAIN -->|Ray storage_path| CK[(training<br/>checkpoints/run_id/)]
  TRAIN -->|rclone sync of output_dir| CK
  TRAIN --> SAMP[(training<br/>samples/run_id/)]
  TRAIN -->|final .safetensors| FIN[(training<br/>runs/run_id/final/)]
  FIN -->|log_artifact b2://| MLF[MLflow tracking + registry]
  FIN -->|dvc push| DVC[DVC remote prefix]
  FIN -->|approved release| REL[(released-weights<br/>Object Lock)]
  SNAP -->|presigned GET of dataset zip| REP[Replicate hosted training]
  REP -->|download weights, PUT| FIN
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Scheduler
  participant G as Spot GPU node
  participant B as B2 training bucket
  S->>G: start run_id
  G->>B: LIST checkpoints/<run_id>/
  alt checkpoint exists
    G->>B: GET latest checkpoint
  end
  loop every N steps
    G->>G: write checkpoint to local NVMe
    G->>B: multipart PUT checkpoints/<run_id>/step-N/
    G->>B: PUT samples/<run_id>/step-N/grid.png
  end
  G->>B: PUT runs/<run_id>/final/*.safetensors
  G->>B: PUT runs/<run_id>/run.json (last)
```

Checkpoints live under a top-level `checkpoints/` prefix rather than inside `runs/<run_id>/` so that one lifecycle rule expires intermediates for every run while `runs/<run_id>/final/` is untouched. B2 lifecycle rules match by file-name prefix and cannot wildcard a run ID.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-imggen-training` | `runs/<run_id>/dataset/`, `runs/<run_id>/captions/`, `runs/<run_id>/run.json` | Keep | No | Snapshot reference, captions, run config and lineage |
| `<org>-imggen-training` | `checkpoints/<run_id>/` | Hide after N days, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-training.json)) | No | Resume points |
| `<org>-imggen-training` | `samples/<run_id>/` | Hide after N days, then delete | No | Sample grids for review |
| `<org>-imggen-training` | `runs/<run_id>/final/` | Keep | No | Final weights before approval |
| `<org>-imggen-training` | `mlflow/`, `dvc/` | Keep | No | MLflow artifacts and DVC cache |
| `<org>-imggen-released-weights` | `weights/<model>/<version>/` | Never overwrite | Governance default retention ([example](examples/object-lock.json)) | Approved releases with model card and license |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Active shards and in-progress checkpoint writes | GPU-node NVMe | Training reads and writes need local-disk latency; upload completed checkpoints |
| MLflow backend store (metrics, params, stages, aliases) | Postgres or MySQL | MLflow keeps metadata in a database; only artifacts go to B2 |
| Job scheduler state | Ray, Slurm or Kubernetes | Coordination state |
| Replicate's transient training storage | Replicate | Outside your control; copy outputs back |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Status | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Used | Ray, MLflow, DVC and boto3 reach `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | Used | Presigned GET of the dataset zip for Replicate; no browser access, so no CORS |
| Multipart upload | Used | Multi-GB checkpoints and full fine-tune weights |
| Scoped application keys | Used | Per-run or per-tenant trainer keys; publisher key for released weights |
| Event Notifications | Not used | Promotion is an explicit approval step |
| Object versions | Used | Released weights are never overwritten |
| Lifecycle rules | Used | Expire `checkpoints/` and `samples/` |
| SSE-B2 | Optional | Enable for proprietary or customer-derived weights ([example](examples/sse.json)) |
| Object Lock | Used | Released-weights bucket only |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | Replicate released weights for DR or a second-region fleet (see [model-weight-distribution](architectures/model-weight-distribution/architecture.md)) |
| Egress / CDN / compute partners | Situational | Run GPUs near the bucket region; see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for egress terms |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard default | Checkpoint writes are periodic; local NVMe is the hot tier. [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) is rarely the bottleneck here |

## Integration configuration

Derive every endpoint from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`.

### Ray Train

Ray's persistent-storage guide has a section for S3-compatible storage that names Backblaze B2. Either pass the endpoint in the URI:

```python
RunConfig(storage_path="s3://<org>-imggen-training/checkpoints?endpoint_override=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com", name=run_id)
```

or set `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` with `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` holding a B2 application key and use a plain `s3://` path. Ray writes checkpoints under `storage_path/name/`, which lands them in `checkpoints/<run_id>/`.

### MLflow

MLflow's artifact-store documentation has a Backblaze B2 section: artifact URI `b2://<bucket>@s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<path>`, with `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` set to a B2 application key and region. Use a B2 application key, not the master key. The backend store and model registry metadata stay in the database.

### DVC

`dvc remote add -d b2 s3://<org>-imggen-training/dvc` then `dvc remote modify b2 endpointurl https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Keep credentials in `dvc remote modify --local` (git-ignored config) or environment variables.

### rclone (local-disk trainers)

diffusers example scripts and kohya sd-scripts write only to a local `output_dir`. rclone's native B2 backend syncs the snapshot in before training and copies checkpoints and finals out after each save. The training worker handles B2 transfers through rclone.

### Replicate (hosted training)

Replicate documents file inputs passed as URLs and deletes API output files after one hour. Pass a presigned B2 GET URL to the dataset zip as the hosted-file input, then download the resulting weights and write them to `runs/<run_id>/final/` before they expire.

### Scoped keys

| Role | Bucket | Prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trainer-<run_id>` | training | `checkpoints/<run_id>/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| `run-writer` | training | `runs/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| `samples-writer` | training | `samples/` | `listFiles,writeFiles` |
| `tracking` (MLflow, DVC) | training | `mlflow/` or `dvc/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles` (only if garbage collection is required) |
| `presign-dataset` | training | `runs/` | `readFiles` |
| `weights-publisher` | released-weights | `weights/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,writeFileRetentions` |

A Ray run that writes checkpoints, sample grids and run metadata uses three prefix-scoped keys, or one bucket-scoped key if your threat model accepts it.

## Security

- Trainers never hold delete rights on released weights; Object Lock enforces retention independently.
- Presigned dataset URLs for hosted training are bearer credentials; set the TTL to cover job start only and never log them.
- Store keys in a secret manager or a gitignored `0600` `.env`; never in `dvc` tracked config or MLflow params.
- Copy large objects (for promotion) with multipart `UploadPartCopy`; check the [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api) for copy size limits.

## References

- [Ray Train persistent storage](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html)
- [MLflow artifact stores](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/)
- [DVC Amazon S3 remote](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3)
- [rclone Backblaze B2](https://rclone.org/b2/)
- [Replicate input files](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files) and [output files](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/output-files)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)

<!-- source: architectures/model-weight-distribution/architecture.md -->

# Distribute base checkpoints and LoRAs to a GPU inference fleet

## Workload

An inference fleet (ComfyUI hosts, diffusers servers, serverless GPU functions) needs base checkpoints, VAEs, ControlNets and a catalog of LoRAs. Base weights are several GB each and LoRA catalogs grow to thousands of files. Pulling from public hubs on every cold start is slow, rate-limited and lets versions drift between nodes.

B2 is the single source of truth for approved weights. Nodes pull into local caches with read-only keys and skip files that have not changed. Runtime model directories, registry metadata and GPU memory stay off B2.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CI[CI / release job<br/>B2 GitHub Action] -->|immutable versioned keys,<br/>latest pointer last| MOD[(models bucket<br/>models/)]
  HF[Hugging Face hub cache] -->|hf-cache-sync push| HFC[(models bucket<br/>hf-cache/team/)]
  MOD -->|Download Model from Cloud<br/>ETag skip| COMFY[ComfyUI host<br/>local models/]
  MOD -->|CloudBucketMount read_only| MODAL[Modal GPU function]
  MOD -->|rclone copy| WARM[New node pre-warm]
  HFC -->|hf-cache-sync pull| DIFF[diffusers server<br/>local HF cache]
  MOD -.->|Cloud Replication| MOD2[(models bucket<br/>second region)]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant N as GPU node
  participant L as Local cache
  participant B as B2 models/
  N->>B: GET models/lora/<name>/latest.json
  N->>L: lookup <name>/<version>
  alt cached and ETag matches HEAD
    N->>L: load from disk
  else missing or changed
    N->>B: GET weights (ranged / parallel)
    N->>N: verify SHA-256 from model card
    N->>L: write, then LRU-prune
  end
```

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-imggen-models` | `models/base/<model>/<version>/` | Keep all versions | Per-file retention set by CI (no bucket default) | Base checkpoints with model card, license, SHA-256 |
| `<org>-imggen-models` | `models/lora/<name>/<version>/` | Keep | Per-file retention set by CI (no bucket default) | LoRA adapters |
| `<org>-imggen-models` | `models/vae/`, `models/controlnet/` | Keep | Per-file retention set by CI (no bucket default) | Auxiliary weights |
| `<org>-imggen-models` | `models/<kind>/<name>/latest.json` | Overwritten on each release | No | Mutable pointer, written last |
| `<org>-imggen-models` | `hf-cache/<team>/` | No lifecycle; prune remote revisions manually or with tooling that knows which blobs are referenced | No | Mirrored Hugging Face hub blobs and refs |
| `<org>-imggen-models-<dr>` | same prefixes | Replica | Object Lock enabled if the source has it | Second-region fleet or DR ([example](examples/replication.json)) |

Immutable versioned keys plus a small mutable pointer let nodes cache by version forever and still find the newest release.

B2 default retention applies to a whole bucket, and this bucket also holds the mutable `latest.json` pointer and deletable `hf-cache/` blobs. If governance requires locking, enable Object Lock on the bucket without a default retention and have CI set retention on each released file version (the B2 GitHub Action's retention option, which needs `writeFileRetentions`). Pointers and cache blobs then stay deletable. If you need a bucket-wide default instead, publish releases to a separate locked bucket, as [diffusion-finetune-checkpoints](architectures/diffusion-finetune-checkpoints/architecture.md) does.

hf-cache-sync stores content-addressed blobs that later revisions can share, and B2 lifecycle rules expire by upload age, not by last access. Its LRU prune applies to the local disk only, so do not put a lifecycle rule on `hf-cache/`.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Model directories the runtime loads from | Node-local NVMe | Loaders expect a local filesystem and fast random reads |
| Model registry metadata (stages, aliases, approvals) | MLflow database or equivalent | Relational state (see [diffusion-finetune-checkpoints](architectures/diffusion-finetune-checkpoints/architecture.md)) |
| ComfyUI workflow JSON | App or git | Shared freely; must contain no credentials |
| Loaded weights | GPU memory | Runtime state |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Status | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Used | All pullers use `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | Not used | Nodes hold read-only keys; no browser access |
| Multipart upload | Used | Multi-GB checkpoints from CI |
| Scoped application keys | Used | CI writes; every worker is read-only on `models/` |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Notify a fleet controller when `latest.json` changes |
| Object versions | Used | Released weights are never overwritten; the pointer is versioned |
| Lifecycle rules | Not used | Never on `models/`; unsafe on `hf-cache/` because blobs are shared across revisions |
| SSE-B2 | Optional | Enable for proprietary weights ([example](examples/sse.json)) |
| Object Lock | Optional | Per-file retention on released weights set by CI; no bucket default retention |
| Cloud Replication | Used for multi-region fleets | Bucket-to-bucket copy to a second region; not a delivery mechanism |
| Egress / CDN / compute partners | Situational | Pulls by nodes outside the region count as egress; see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Local cache first | Node caches remove repeat reads. Measure fleet-wide cold starts that pull the same large files at once before considering [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) |

## Integration configuration

Derive every endpoint from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`.

### ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes

The README documents a "Backblaze B2" provider preset (`COMFY_S3_PROVIDER`, `COMFY_S3_REGION`) or `COMFY_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` for a custom endpoint. Credentials resolve from environment variables or a server-side JSON profile and never appear in workflow JSON. The Download Model from Cloud node pulls into the correct local `models/` directory and skips the download when the remote ETag matches. Read-only access comes from the B2 key you configure, not from the node.

### hf-cache-sync

Configure `storage.endpoint` in YAML, or `B2_ENDPOINT`, `B2_BUCKET` and `B2_REGION` with `B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID` / `B2_APPLICATION_KEY`. It pushes content-addressed blobs and revision manifests and prunes the local cache by LRU.

### Modal CloudBucketMount

```python
modal.CloudBucketMount(
    "<org>-imggen-models",
    bucket_endpoint_url="https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com",
    key_prefix="models/",
    read_only=True,
    secret=modal.Secret.from_name("b2-models-reader"),  # AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = B2 key
)
```

Set `bucket_endpoint_url` to the B2 endpoint and put a read-only B2 application key in the Modal secret. The mount is a network filesystem: for multi-GB weights, copy to the container's local disk at startup rather than loading lazily on the first request.

### rclone

The native B2 backend handles bulk migration of existing checkpoint libraries and pre-warms new nodes (`rclone copy b2:<bucket>/models/base/<model>/<version> /models/...`).

### Publishing from CI

The [Backblaze B2 GitHub Action](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/b2-action) uploads with multipart, verifies SHA-1 and sets Object Lock retention. Upload the version first, then overwrite `latest.json`.

### Scoped keys

| Role | Bucket | Prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-publisher` | models | `models/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` (+ `writeFileRetentions` if locking) |
| `fleet-reader` | models | `models/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| `hf-cache-<team>` | models | `hf-cache/<team>/` | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles` |

## Security

- Only CI holds write keys; a compromised GPU node cannot replace weights.
- Verify SHA-256 from the model card or manifest after download. Multipart ETags are not content MD5s, so ETags are compared for change detection only.
- B2's S3-compatible API does not fully support object tagging; keep model metadata in the card or pointer file, not in tags.
- Never embed credentials in shareable ComfyUI workflows.

## References

- [ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage)
- [hf-cache-sync](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/hf-cache-sync)
- [Modal CloudBucketMount reference](https://modal.com/docs/reference/modal.CloudBucketMount) and [cloud bucket mounts guide](https://modal.com/docs/guide/cloud-bucket-mounts)
- [rclone Backblaze B2](https://rclone.org/b2/)
- [B2 Cloud Replication](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cloud-replication)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)

<!-- source: architectures/generation-output-provenance/architecture.md -->

# Generate images and persist every output with provenance manifests

## Workload

Text-to-image and image-editing applications call self-hosted pipelines (ComfyUI, diffusers) or hosted APIs (for example OpenAI gpt-image-1, Google Imagen, or FLUX through Replicate, fal.ai or NVIDIA NIM). Every output must be kept: users return to galleries, remix earlier images, and trust and safety teams audit what was generated, from which prompt and model. Hosted APIs return URLs that expire, so an app that only stores those URLs loses its images.

B2 is the system of record for generated bytes and their provenance manifests. Queues, billing, user databases and caches stay elsewhere.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  USER[User / app] -->|prompt + refs| APP[App server]
  APP -->|presigned GET of inputs/| PROV[Hosted API<br/>fal.ai / Replicate / NIM / OpenAI]
  APP --> SELF[Self-hosted pipeline<br/>ComfyUI / diffusers]
  PROV -->|ephemeral output URL or bytes| SINK[Output persistence worker]
  SELF -->|Save to Cloud node| OUT
  SINK -->|image + manifest.json| OUT[(outputs bucket<br/>runs/tenant/date/run_id/)]
  OUT -.->|approved manifest| PUB[Audit publisher<br/>separate audit credential]
  PUB --> AUD[(audit bucket<br/>Object Lock)]
  OUT -->|ObjectCreated event| IDX[Indexer<br/>app DB or Pixeltable]
  OUT -->|presigned GET| VIEW[User gallery / share link]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as App
  participant P as Hosted API
  participant B as B2 outputs
  A->>B: presign GET inputs/<tenant>/<ref>.png (short TTL)
  A->>P: generate(prompt, image_url=presigned)
  P-->>A: output URL (expires)
  A->>P: GET output bytes
  A->>A: sha256(bytes)
  A->>B: PUT runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/<sha256>.png
  A->>B: PUT runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/manifest.json (last)
```

A manifest records provider, model, prompt, parameters, seed, timestamps, parent asset (for remixes and edits) and the SHA-256 of each output. Writing it last makes it the commit marker: a run without a manifest is incomplete.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-imggen-outputs` | `inputs/<tenant>/` | Hide after N days, then delete | No | Reference images handed to providers |
| `<org>-imggen-outputs` | `runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/` | Keep current; purge hidden versions | No | Outputs and `manifest.json` per run |
| `<org>-imggen-outputs` | `assets/<sha256>` | Keep | No | Optional content-addressed layout (dedupes remixes) |
| `<org>-imggen-outputs` | `drafts/<tenant>/` | Hide after N days, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-outputs.json)) | No | Abandoned or unselected variants |
| `<org>-imggen-audit` | `manifests/<tenant>/<date>/` | Never overwrite | Governance default retention ([example](examples/object-lock.json)) | Audit copy of manifests when policy requires immutability |

User outputs stay deletable; the audit bucket holds only manifests, so a user deletion does not conflict with retention of the audit trail. Decide with counsel whether manifests contain personal data (prompts can) before locking them.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Request queue and GPU worker state | Redis, SQS or a job runner | Low-latency coordination |
| Rate limits, credits and billing | App database | Transactional |
| Users, galleries and prompt history | SQLite or Postgres (as in the samples) | Queried and edited per request |
| Prompt and result caches | Redis or memory | Latency |
| C2PA signing keys | KMS or HSM | Keys never sit next to the assets they sign |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Status | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Used | Application workers, ComfyUI nodes and Pixeltable write through `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | Used | Presigned GET for provider inputs and private share links; CORS only if browsers fetch with JavaScript |
| Multipart upload | Not needed | Outputs are small; single PUT |
| Scoped application keys | Used | Per-tenant prefix keys or a signer that enforces the tenant prefix |
| Event Notifications | Used | `b2:ObjectCreated:*` on `runs/` triggers indexing and moderation |
| Object versions | Used | Purge hidden versions on user deletion |
| Lifecycle rules | Used | Expire `drafts/` and `inputs/` |
| SSE-B2 | Recommended | Default encryption for user content ([example](examples/sse.json)) |
| Object Lock | Used (audit bucket only) | Immutable manifests where policy requires them |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | DR copy of the audit bucket |
| Egress / CDN / compute partners | Used | Public galleries go through a CDN (see [gallery-cdn-delivery](architectures/gallery-cdn-delivery/architecture.md)) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard | Many small objects; request rate, not bandwidth, dominates |

## Integration configuration

Derive every endpoint from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`.

### Optional implementation example: Genblaze

[Genblaze](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze#storage) is one SDK option for the persistence worker. After installing it and configuring a generation pipeline, set `B2_BUCKET` to the private outputs bucket and supply `B2_REGION`, `B2_KEY_ID` and `B2_APP_KEY` through the service environment:

```python
import os
from genblaze_core import KeyStrategy, ObjectStorageSink
from genblaze_s3 import S3StorageBackend

storage = ObjectStorageSink(
    S3StorageBackend.for_backblaze(os.environ["B2_BUCKET"]),
    prefix="",
    key_strategy=KeyStrategy.HIERARCHICAL,
)
# Pass this sink to the configured pipeline: pipeline.run(sink=storage).
```

Set the run's `tenant_id` from authenticated application context. This configuration writes assets and `manifest.json` under `runs/<tenant>/<date>/<run_id>/`; the default SDK layout uses a different root and content-addressed keys. Grant `listBuckets` for its `HeadBucket` preflight. Always transfer output bytes through the sink so the manifest covers their SHA-256 hashes. Keep durable bucket/key/hash references in provenance and presign private objects at read time. The audit publisher copies approved manifests to the separate audit bucket with its own credential; the sink does not perform that cross-bucket step.

### ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes

Save Image to Cloud writes graph outputs under a `key_prefix` and can return a presigned URL (`presign_url`, `expires_hours`). Use the "Backblaze B2" provider preset. Credentials resolve server-side and never appear in workflow JSON.

### fal.ai

fal's CDN documentation states that presigned S3 or R2 URLs work as file inputs because authentication is embedded in the URL. Pass short-TTL presigned B2 GETs as `image_url` and copy outputs to B2 on completion.

### Replicate

Replicate accepts file inputs as URLs and deletes API output files after one hour. Copy outputs to B2 in the completion handler or webhook, and pass private inputs as short-expiry presigned B2 GET URLs.

### Pixeltable

Pixeltable's cloud-storage documentation has a Backblaze B2 section: destination `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<bucket>/<prefix>/`, `b2_profile` in `config.toml`, keys in a `[b2]` AWS credentials profile. Use it to index outputs and computed columns; the bucket stays the system of record.

### Scoped keys

| Role | Bucket | Prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generator-<tenant>` | outputs | `runs/<tenant>/` | `listBuckets,listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` (`listBuckets` supports SDK preflight) |
| `input-writer` (app upload path, or presigned PUT) | outputs | `inputs/` | `writeFiles` |
| `input-signer` | outputs | `inputs/` | `readFiles` |
| `indexer` | outputs | `runs/` | `listFiles,readFiles` |
| `audit-writer` | audit | `manifests/` | `listFiles,writeFiles` |

For many tenants, one server-side key per service plus a signer that refuses object keys outside the caller's tenant prefix is simpler than one B2 key per tenant.

## Security

- Providers receive presigned GETs with short TTLs, never application keys.
- Treat share links as bearer credentials; log their issuance, not the URLs.
- Verify `X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature` on indexing webhooks; make handlers idempotent.
- Moderate before outputs become public.

## References

- [Genblaze](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/genblaze)
- [ComfyUI Cloud Storage nodes](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/comfyui-cloud-storage)
- [fal CDN and file inputs](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/fal-cdn)
- [Replicate input files](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files) and [output files](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/output-files)
- [Pixeltable cloud storage](https://docs.pixeltable.com/integrations/cloud-storage)
- [B2 Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)

<!-- source: architectures/user-upload-moderation-personalization/architecture.md -->

# Ingest, moderate and purge user-uploaded reference images

## Workload

Personalization apps (avatars, headshots, product photography, style transfer) take user uploads: selfies, product shots, reference images. Uploads are personal and sometimes biometric-adjacent. They must be moderated before use, reach model providers only briefly, expire on schedule, and be deletable per subject on request.

B2 holds uploads, moderation outcomes and per-subject outputs. Browsers upload directly to B2 with presigned PUTs, so image bytes never pass through app servers. Auth, consent records, moderation decisions and workers stay elsewhere.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  BR[Browser<br/>Uppy] -->|1. request upload| API[App API / Companion]
  API -->|2. presigned PUT<br/>uploads/tenant/subject/| BR
  BR -->|3. PUT image| UP[(uploads bucket<br/>uploads/)]
  UP -->|4. ObjectCreated event, signed| HOOK[Webhook receiver]
  HOOK -->|enqueue| MOD[Moderation worker<br/>NSFW classifier + EXIF strip]
  MOD -->|PUT stripped copy| APR[(approved/tenant/subject/)]
  MOD -->|server-side copy| QUA[(quarantine/tenant/subject/batch/)]
  MOD -->|JSONL| LOG[(audit/moderation/tenant/subject/)]
  APR -->|short-TTL presigned GET| PROV[fal.ai edit / Replicate LoRA training]
  PROV -->|outputs copied back| OUT[(subjects/tenant/subject/outputs/)]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant A as App and consent DB
  participant P as Provider adapters
  participant B as B2 uploads bucket
  U->>A: Delete my data (authenticated tenant and subject)
  A->>A: Mark deleting atomically; block new signing and writer leases
  A->>A: Cancel or drain active uploads, multipart sessions and jobs
  A->>P: Cancel active jobs; delete stored inputs, outputs and trained artifacts
  P-->>A: Deletion confirmed or documented retention expiry reached
  A->>B: ListObjectVersions for uploads, approved, quarantine, subjects and audit subject prefixes
  loop Every version and delete marker, including inventory keys
    A->>B: DeleteObject(key, versionId)
  end
  A->>A: Reconcile late completions under the subject tombstone; repeat cleanup
  A->>B: ListObjectVersions (all subject prefixes) returns empty
  A->>A: Complete only when writers are closed and required provider copies are gone
  A->>A: Record purge request ID, outcome and completion time
```

Approval is a read, strip EXIF (including GPS), then PutObject of the stripped bytes to `approved/<tenant>/<subject>/`. A server-side copy would carry the original metadata to providers, so it is used only for `quarantine/`, where the original bytes are kept for appeal and never presigned. The event rule watches `uploads/` only, so copies into `approved/` and `quarantine/` do not retrigger moderation.

## Subject deletion coordination

The app database stores the subject state (`active`, `deleting`, `deleted`) and an inventory of B2 object keys, version IDs, provider request IDs, and generated model/artifact IDs. Use opaque tenant and subject identifiers in keys. The inventory includes quarantined originals, moderation records, generated outputs, and trained weights.

A deletion request atomically marks the subject `deleting` and prevents new upload URLs, provider handoffs, and worker write leases. Cancel or drain existing uploads and jobs before final reconciliation, including multipart sessions. Workers and event handlers consult the tombstone before committing outputs; late uploads or callbacks are routed to cleanup. Presigned-URL expiry alone does not establish that an upload already in progress has finished.

The purge coordinator uses `writeFiles` to abort multipart uploads and `deleteFiles` to remove stored versions. Keep its credential in the cleanup service. See the [S3 capability mapping](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-app-keys).

Each provider adapter records how copied inputs, outputs, and trained artifacts are deleted or expire under that provider's retention policy. Cancel active work, request deletion where available, and retain a pending purge until deletion is acknowledged or the documented data-retention deadline has passed. Expiring a B2 input URL does not delete a provider's copy. A training artifact or model version has its own deletion record.

Delete all versions and delete markers under `uploads/<tenant>/<subject>/`, `approved/<tenant>/<subject>/`, `quarantine/<tenant>/<subject>/`, `subjects/<tenant>/<subject>/`, and `audit/moderation/<tenant>/<subject>/`, plus any additional keys in the inventory. Repeat listings after reconciling late work. Purge retries are idempotent; unresolved writers or provider records keep the request pending. Retain the tombstone to reject retries, and keep only the required deletion receipt under an explicit audit-retention policy.

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-imggen-uploads` | `uploads/<tenant>/<subject>/` | Hide after N days, then delete ([example](examples/lifecycle-uploads.json)) | **No** | Raw browser uploads |
| `<org>-imggen-uploads` | `approved/<tenant>/<subject>/` | Expire after training per consent | No | EXIF-stripped, moderated references |
| `<org>-imggen-uploads` | `quarantine/<tenant>/<subject>/<batch>/` | Hide after review window, then delete | No | Rejected items held for appeal |
| `<org>-imggen-uploads` | `subjects/<tenant>/<subject>/outputs/` | Per product retention | No | Generated results for the subject |
| `<org>-imggen-uploads` | `audit/moderation/<tenant>/<subject>/` | Delete with the subject | No | Subject-scoped moderation records (no image bytes) |

Do not enable Object Lock on this bucket. Locked versions cannot be deleted before retention ends, so per-subject purge would fail. SSE-B2 default encryption ([example](examples/sse.json)) and CORS for the app origin ([example](examples/cors.json)) apply bucket-wide.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Auth and user database | App database | Transactional |
| Consent, subject state, object/provider inventory and purge receipts | App database | Coordinates writers, provider cleanup and deletion retries |
| Moderation decisions and appeals | App database | Queried by reviewers |
| Processing queue | Redis, SQS or similar | The webhook must acknowledge fast |
| Classifier workers | GPU or CPU pool | Compute |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Status | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Used | Companion, workers and signer use `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | Used | Presigned PUT for uploads, presigned GET for providers; CORS restricted to the app origin |
| Multipart upload | Optional | Companion can use multipart for large files; selfies rarely need it |
| Scoped application keys | Used | Signer, moderator, provider-signer, purger (below) |
| Event Notifications | Used | `b2:ObjectCreated:*` on `uploads/` to a signed webhook ([example](examples/event-notifications.json)) |
| Object versions | Used | Purge deletes every version |
| Lifecycle rules | Used | Expire raw uploads and quarantine |
| SSE-B2 | Used | Default bucket encryption |
| Object Lock | Deliberately not used | Would block verifiable deletion |
| Cloud Replication | Deliberately not used | A replica doubles the purge surface; deletes and hide markers are not replicated |
| Egress / CDN / compute partners | Not used | Uploads are private; never cache them on a CDN |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard | Small objects, request-bound |

## Integration configuration

Derive every endpoint from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`.

### Uppy + Companion

Companion documents `s3.endpoint` (`COMPANION_AWS_ENDPOINT`) as an optional URL to a custom S3-compatible service. Point it at the B2 endpoint, set the bucket and region, and give it a key that can only write `uploads/`. Uploads go from the browser directly to B2 with presigned requests. Companion's `getKey` hook should build `uploads/<tenant>/<subject>/<uuid>` from the authenticated session, never from client input.

### fal.ai

fal's CDN documentation states that presigned S3 or R2 URLs work as file inputs. Pass short-TTL presigned GETs of `approved/` objects as `image_url`; copy outputs to `subjects/<tenant>/<subject>/outputs/`.

### Replicate

Pass a presigned GET of a zip of approved images as the training input (the [AI Headshot Studio](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/ai-headshot-studio) sample uses this for FLUX LoRA training). Replicate accepts hosted files by URL, so a presigned B2 GET works as the input. Copy trained weights back to B2 before Replicate's output files expire.

### Event Notifications

Configure a rule on `uploads/` for `b2:ObjectCreated:Upload` and `b2:ObjectCreated:MultipartUpload` with an HMAC signing secret. The receiver verifies `X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature`, enqueues, and responds quickly (the B2 reference guide's example acknowledges within three seconds). Handlers must be idempotent. The [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker) sample shows fan-out to several subscribers.

### Scoped keys

| Role | Bucket | Prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upload-signer` (Companion) | uploads | `uploads/` | `writeFiles` |
| `moderator` | uploads | (bucket) | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` |
| `provider-signer` | uploads | `approved/` | `readFiles` |
| `purger` | uploads | (bucket) | `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles` |
| `notifications-admin` (provisioning only) | uploads | (bucket) | `readBucketNotifications,writeBucketNotifications` |

## Security

- Application keys never reach browsers; presigned PUTs are scoped to one key and expire quickly.
- Strip EXIF, including GPS, before any third-party handoff.
- Quarantined items are never presigned for providers.
- Complete purge only after writer reconciliation, provider cleanup, and an empty all-version listing across every subject prefix. Log the purge request ID, outcome, and completion time; retain identifiers only under the audit policy.
- Keep the signing secret for event webhooks in a secret store.

## References

- [Uppy Companion](https://uppy.io/docs/companion/)
- [fal CDN and file inputs](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/fal-cdn)
- [Replicate input files](https://replicate.com/docs/topics/predictions/input-files)
- [B2 Event Notifications reference](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide)
- [B2 CORS rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cross-origin-resource-sharing-rules)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 server-side encryption](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-server-side-encryption)

<!-- source: architectures/gallery-cdn-delivery/architecture.md -->

# Serve generated galleries through a CDN with on-the-fly variants

## Workload

Generated-image galleries, community feeds and marketplaces are read-heavy, with long-tail access to old generations. Each image is shown at several sizes and formats. Storing every thumbnail size multiplies object counts, and serving everything directly from origin makes egress unpredictable.

B2 stores one original per image in a private bucket. A CDN fronts it, signs origin requests with a read-only key, and caches variants that imgproxy produces on request. Feeds, counters and caches stay elsewhere.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  VIEW[Browser] -->|/img/w_512/key.webp| CDN[CDN edge<br/>Cloudflare / bunny.net / Fastly]
  CDN -->|cache miss| IMGP[imgproxy<br/>signed URLs]
  IMGP -->|S3 GET, read-only key| PUB[(gallery bucket<br/>public/)]
  CDN -->|originals, cache miss<br/>SigV4 Worker or S3 auth pull zone| PUB
  PRIV[Private item] -->|short-TTL presigned GET| VIEW
  PUB -->|unpublish: delete or hide| EV[ObjectDeleted / HideMarkerCreated event]
  EV --> PURGE[CDN cache purge]
```

## B2 zones

| Bucket | Prefix | Versioning / lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<org>-imggen-gallery` | `public/<tenant>/<id>.<ext>` | Keep current; purge hidden versions after N days | No | Approved originals served through the CDN, with `Cache-Control` set at upload |
| `<org>-imggen-gallery` | `private/<tenant>/<id>.<ext>` | Keep | No | Items served only by presigned URL |

Variants are not stored. The source of each item (its run and manifest) stays in the outputs bucket from [generation-output-provenance](architectures/generation-output-provenance/architecture.md); promotion reads the approved original with an outputs-bucket reader key and PUTs it here with the gallery `promoter` key. A cross-bucket server-side copy would need one key with read on the source and write on the destination, which breaks the one-bucket, one-prefix key rule; gallery images are small, so the extra transfer is the cheaper trade-off.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Edge cache of originals and variants | CDN | Serves the read volume |
| imgproxy cache | imgproxy or CDN | Re-derivable |
| Gallery and feed database, search index | App database or search service | Queried per request |
| Like and view counters | Redis or app database | High write rate, mutable |
| Worker secrets | CDN secret store | The read-only key never ships in code |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Status | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Used | Worker, pull zone and imgproxy read from `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` |
| Presigned URLs / CORS | Used | Presigned GET for private items; CORS only if the front end fetches images with JavaScript |
| Multipart upload | Not needed | Originals are small |
| Scoped application keys | Used | Read-only keys scoped to `public/` for the CDN and imgproxy |
| Event Notifications | Optional | `b2:ObjectDeleted:*` or `b2:HideMarkerCreated:*` on `public/` triggers CDN purge |
| Object versions | Used | Purge hidden versions after unpublish |
| Lifecycle rules | Used | Delete hidden versions after N days ([example](examples/lifecycle-gallery.json)) |
| SSE-B2 | Optional | Transparent to the CDN path |
| Object Lock | Deliberately not used | Takedowns must take effect |
| Cloud Replication | Not used | The CDN absorbs read load; replicate only for DR |
| Egress / CDN / compute partners | Used | B2 offers free egress to CDN partners including Cloudflare, Fastly and bunny.net; confirm current terms on [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard + CDN cache | Cache hit rate decides origin load; [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) is not usually the bottleneck |

## Integration configuration

Derive every endpoint from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`.

### Cloudflare (Worker for a private bucket)

Backblaze's guide deploys a Worker that SigV4-signs requests to the private bucket's S3 endpoint with a read-only application key stored as Worker secrets. The [cloudflare-b2](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/cloudflare-b2) sample is the reference implementation. Cloudflare is a Bandwidth Alliance partner, which is the basis for free egress on this path.

### bunny.net

bunny.net documents Backblaze B2 as a pull zone origin ([bunny.net guide](https://docs.bunny.net/cdn/integrations/storage/backblaze)). Set the origin to the bucket's S3 URL and enable S3 Authentication with the key ID as access key, the application key as secret, and the bucket's region. Backblaze recommends enabling **Block Root Path Access** so the pull zone does not return a bucket listing.

### Fastly

Deploy the [fastly-b2-rust](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/fastly-b2-rust) sample: a Fastly Compute app that signs origin requests to a private bucket with a read-only application key.

### imgproxy

imgproxy documents S3 sources: `IMGPROXY_USE_S3=true`, `IMGPROXY_S3_ENDPOINT=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, `IMGPROXY_S3_REGION=<region>`, and source URLs of the form `s3://<bucket>/<key>`. Its documentation covers MinIO through the same endpoint option. Path-style addressing is the default. Restrict sources with `IMGPROXY_S3_ALLOWED_BUCKETS` and enable URL signing (`IMGPROXY_KEY`, `IMGPROXY_SALT`).

### Scoped keys

| Role | Bucket | Prefix | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cdn-origin` | gallery | `public/` | `readFiles` (add `listFiles` only if the CDN needs it) |
| `imgproxy-reader` | gallery | `public/` | `readFiles` |
| `private-signer` | gallery | `private/` | `readFiles` |
| `promoter` | gallery | `public/` | `writeFiles,deleteFiles` |
| `promoter-source` | outputs | `runs/` | `readFiles` |

## Security

- The bucket stays private; only signed CDN and imgproxy requests reach it.
- Signed imgproxy URLs stop the transformer from being used as an open proxy or a resize-amplification target.
- Private items never go through shared CDN caches; use presigned URLs with short TTLs.
- Purge CDN caches on unpublish and takedown.
